title: MODALES DE DEDUCCIÓN
subtitle: Modals of deduction · must, might, can't

map.center: Usamos MUST, MIGHT, COULD, CAN'T para deducir: decir lo seguros que estamos de algo, ahora o en el pasado.

nodes.title: Presente
items: She must be at home. (Debe de estar en casa.)

nodes.title: Consejo rápido
items: Pista → conclusión: The lights are off. → They must be out.

mini.es: Completa con must, might o can't.
mini.en: Complete with must, might or can't.

items.q: Her lights are on. She ___ be in.
He's only 15. He ___ be a doctor!
Take an umbrella. It ___ rain.
The road is wet. It ___ have rained.
I ___ have left my keys at work. Not sure.

explain.es: Los modales de deducción sirven para sacar conclusiones a partir de pistas, como un detective. No hablan de obligación ni de habilidad, sino de lo seguros que estamos. En español usamos deber de, seguro que, a lo mejor, puede que, no puede ser que o el futuro de probabilidad (Estará en casa · Serán las tres). En inglés lo normal es usar un modal.
explain.en: Modals of deduction help us to draw conclusions from evidence. They show how sure we are that something is true, now or in the past.

explain.title: El termómetro de la certeza
head: Modal
Certeza · Certainty
En español
rows: debe de, seguro que, tiene que
no puede ser que, es imposible
explain.note: Si estás 100 % seguro, no uses modal: She is at home (lo sé). El modal es para deducir.
explain.note_en: If you are 100% sure, don't use a modal.

explain.title: 1 · MUST: seguro que sí
explain.es: Usamos must cuando tenemos una pista fuerte y estamos casi seguros de que algo es verdad. Equivale a debe de / seguro que / tiene que o al futuro de probabilidad (estará). ¡Ojo! Aquí must no es obligación.
explain.en: We use must when we have strong evidence and we're almost sure something is true. Here, must is not an obligation.

examples.en: You've been travelling all day. You must be exhausted.
examples.es: Llevas todo el día viajando. Debes de estar agotado.

examples.en: There's a queue round the block. That restaurant must be good.
examples.es: Hay cola hasta la esquina. Ese restaurante tiene que ser bueno.

examples.en: Ana isn't answering. She must be in a meeting.
examples.es: Ana no contesta. Estará en una reunión.

explain.title: 2 · MAY, MIGHT, COULD: quizás
explain.es: Para algo posible pero no seguro. may, might y could significan casi lo mismo: puede que, a lo mejor, quizás. might es el más frecuente al hablar; may suena algo más formal. Detrás va el infinitivo: en español usamos subjuntivo (puede que esté), en inglés no.
explain.en: For something possible but not certain. May, might and could mean almost the same. After them, use the infinitive.

examples.en: Don't wait for me. I might be late.
examples.es: No me esperes. Puede que llegue tarde.

examples.en: Take a jacket. It could get cold tonight.
examples.es: Llévate una chaqueta. Podría hacer frío esta noche.

examples.en: The flight may be delayed because of the storm.
examples.es: Puede que el vuelo se retrase por la tormenta.

explain.title: 3 · CAN'T / COULDN'T: imposible
explain.es: Cuando estamos seguros de que algo NO es verdad, usamos can't (o couldn't). Es el contrario de must. ¡Nunca mustn't! mustn't es prohibición (no debes), no deducción. En preguntas usamos can o could: Where can she be? · Could it be true?
explain.en: When we're sure something is not true, we use can't or couldn't, never mustn't. In questions: Where can she be? Could it be true?

examples.en: That can't be Javi. He's on holiday in Peru.
examples.es: Ese no puede ser Javi. Está de vacaciones en Perú.

examples.en: You can't be hungry! You've just had lunch.
examples.es: ¡No puedes tener hambre! Acabas de comer.

examples.en: It can't be true. I don't believe it.
examples.es: No puede ser verdad. No me lo creo.

explain.title: Los negativos: ¡cuidado!
head: Forma
Significado
Ejemplo
rows: He can't be ill. I saw him at the gym.
It couldn't be him. He's abroad.

explain.title: 4 · Ahora mismo: modal + be + -ing
explain.es: Para deducir lo que alguien está haciendo en este momento: must / might / can't + be + -ing. En español: estará + gerundio o puede que esté + gerundio.
explain.en: To guess what someone <mark>is doing right now</mark>: must / might / can't + be + -ing.

examples.en: Leo isn't picking up. He must be driving.
examples.es: Leo no lo coge. Estará conduciendo.
¡Chis! Puede que el bebé esté durmiendo.

explain.title: 5 · Deducción en pasado: modal + have + participio
explain.title_en: Past deduction: modal + have + past participle
explain.es: Para sacar conclusiones sobre algo que ya pasó: must have (seguro que sí), may / might / could have (quizás), can't / couldn't have (imposible) + participio. have no cambia nunca (has) y se pronuncia débil: must've /ˈmʌstəv/.
explain.en: To make deductions about the past: must have / might have / can't have + past participle. Have never changes.

examples.en: The streets are wet. It must have rained last night.
examples.es: Las calles están mojadas. Debe de haber llovido anoche.

examples.en: I can't find my wallet. I might have left it in the taxi.
examples.es: No encuentro la cartera. Puede que me la haya dejado en el taxi.

examples.en: She can't have seen my message. Her phone was off.
examples.es: No puede haber visto mi mensaje. Tenía el móvil apagado.

explain.title: Truco del detective
explain.es: Piensa como Sherlock: pista → conclusión. Y si en español usarías el futuro o el condicional de probabilidad (estará, habrá ido, serían las diez), en inglés usa must / might / can't: Estará en casa → She must be at home. Habrá perdido el tren → He must have missed the train.
explain.en: Think like Sherlock: evidence → conclusion. Spanish 'estará / habrá ido' = must be / must have gone.

explain.title: MUST: ¿obligación o deducción?
explain.es: must tiene dos caras. Si hay una pista y sacas una conclusión, es deducción. Pero el contrario de la deducción es can't: mustn't solo significa prohibición.
explain.en: If there's evidence and you draw a conclusion, must is deduction. Its opposite is can't; mustn't only means prohibition.

head: Español
English

explain.note_en: Spanish 'future of probability' → must / might / can't.

explain.title: ¿Cómo deduzco?
explain.title_en: How do I make a deduction?

items.es: Decide la certeza: casi seguro que sí → must · quizás → may / might / could · seguro que no → can't / couldn't.
items.en: Decide how sure you are: must / might / can't.

items.es: ¿Hablas de ahora? → modal + infinitivo. ¿De algo en curso? → modal + be + -ing.
items.en: Present → modal + infinitive. In progress → modal + be + -ing.

items.es: ¿Hablas del pasado? → modal + have + participio (must have gone). Repasa: sin to, sin -s, nunca has.
items.en: Past → modal + have + past participle. No to, no -s, never has.
Someone's knocking. It must be the delivery driver.
items.es: Llaman a la puerta. Será el repartidor.

items.en: Carlos might be at the gym. He usually goes on Mondays.
items.es: Puede que Carlos esté en el gimnasio. Suele ir los lunes.

items.en: This can't be the right address. It's a car park!
items.es: Esta no puede ser la dirección. ¡Es un aparcamiento!

items.en: They must have won the match. Listen to the fans!
items.es: Deben de haber ganado el partido. ¡Escucha a la afición!

items.en: He couldn't have stolen the money. He was with me all night.
items.es: No puede haber robado el dinero. Estuvo conmigo toda la noche.

items.en: I may have made a mistake in the report.
items.es: Puede que haya cometido un error en el informe.

items.en: She might not have got your email. Check the address.
items.es: Puede que no le haya llegado tu correo. Revisa la dirección.

items.en: The meeting must have finished. Everyone's leaving.
items.es: La reunión debe de haber terminado. Todos se están yendo.

items.en: It could be a virus. You should see a doctor.
items.es: Podría ser un virus. Deberías ir al médico.

items.en: They can't have gone far. Their car is still here.
items.es: No pueden haber ido muy lejos. Su coche sigue aquí.

items.en: The shop might be closed on Sundays. Let's check online.
items.es: Puede que la tienda cierre los domingos. Mirémoslo en internet.

items.bad: He mustn't be at home. The lights are off.
items.good: He can't be at home. The lights are off.
items.why: «Seguro que no» = can't. Mustn't es prohibición.
Después de un modal, infinitivo sin to.

items.why_en: have + past participle, not past simple.

items.bad: He must be at home yesterday.
items.good: He must have been at home yesterday.
items.why: Para el pasado: must have + participio.

items.bad: I'm not sure, but I must have left it at home.
items.good: I'm not sure, but I might have left it at home.
items.why: Si no estás seguro → might / may / could, no must.

lines.en: Her coat isn't here, so she must have gone out.

lines.en: Look, her coffee's still warm. She can't have gone far.
lines.es: Mira, su café sigue caliente. No puede haber ido muy lejos.

lines.en: She could have gone to the bakery. She sometimes buys croissants for everyone.
lines.es: Puede que haya ido a la panadería. A veces compra cruasanes para todos.

lines.en: Here she comes… with a big box. You must be a mind reader!
lines.es: Aquí viene… con una caja grande. ¡Debes de leer la mente!

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el caso del inspector Ruiz. Marca T o F y contesta.
exercises.en: Read the story. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
exercises.text_title: The mystery of the empty flat
text: When Inspector Ruiz arrived at flat 4B, the door was open and nobody was inside. The TV was still on and there was a cup of tea on the table. It was still warm, so the owner, Mr Hall, couldn't have left more than ten minutes earlier.

His coat and umbrella were gone, and it was raining heavily, so he must have gone out. 'He might have gone to the shop on the corner,' said the neighbour. 'He often goes there in the evening.' But the inspector shook his head. 'He can't have gone shopping. His wallet is here on the sofa.'

Then Ruiz noticed a train ticket for Edinburgh on the floor. It was for the 8.15 train. 'It's eight o'clock now. He must be on his way to the station,' he said. 'He could still be in a taxi. Let's go!'

items.q: The inspector thinks Mr Hall left a long time ago.
items.why: The tea was still warm, so he couldn't have left more than ten minutes earlier.

items.q: The neighbour is sure Mr Hall went to the shop.
items.why: She says he might have gone.

items.q: Mr Hall took his wallet with him.
items.why: His wallet is on the sofa.

items.q: Why does the inspector think Mr Hall must have gone out?
items.a: Because his coat and umbrella were gone (and it was raining).

items.q: Why can't he have gone shopping?
items.a: Because his wallet is on the sofa.

items.q: Where does the inspector think Mr Hall is now?
items.a: On his way to the station (maybe still in a taxi).

items.q: Copy a deduction about the present from the last paragraph.
a: He must be on his way to the station.
He could still be in a taxi.

items.q: Rewrite with a modal: 'Perhaps he went to the shop.'
items.a: He might (may / could) have gone to the shop.

checklist.es: Uso must cuando estoy casi seguro: She must be tired.
checklist.en: I use must when I'm almost sure.
I use may / might / could for possibilities.
I use can't for impossible things, never mustn't.
